title: Arguments as numbers
description:
Arguments arrive as text. Write the parsing a tool needs:

| Function | Returns |
|---|---|
| `is_number(s)` | 1 if `s` is an optional `-` followed by at least one digit and nothing else, else 0 |
| `to_number(s)` | the value of such a string as a signed 64-bit number, or 0 if it is not one |
| `sum_numbers(s)` | the sum of every number in a string of numbers separated by single spaces, like `"10 -3 25"`; parts that are not numbers are skipped |

Values fit in 64 bits; no overflow checks are needed.

starter.solution.asm:
is_number:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

to_number:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

sum_numbers:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
; parse_part(rdi = start) -> rax = value, rdx = 1 if the part up to a space or the end is a number, rdi = where it stopped
parse_part:
        xor     eax, eax
        xor     r8d, r8d                ; negative?
        xor     r9d, r9d                ; digits seen
        xor     edx, edx
        cmp     byte [rdi], '-'
        jne     .digit
        mov     r8d, 1
        inc     rdi
.digit: movzx   ecx, byte [rdi]
        test    cl, cl
        jz      .end
        cmp     cl, ' '
        je      .end
        sub     ecx, '0'
        cmp     ecx, 9
        ja      .bad
        imul    rax, rax, 10
        add     rax, rcx
        inc     r9
        inc     rdi
        jmp     .digit
.bad:   movzx   ecx, byte [rdi]         ; skip to the end of this part
        test    cl, cl
        jz      .fail
        cmp     cl, ' '
        je      .fail
        inc     rdi
        jmp     .bad
.end:   test    r9, r9
        jz      .fail
        test    r8, r8
        jz      .ok
        neg     rax
.ok:    mov     edx, 1
        ret
.fail:  xor     eax, eax
        xor     edx, edx
        ret

is_number:
        call    parse_part
        test    edx, edx
        jz      .no
        cmp     byte [rdi], 0
        jne     .no
        mov     eax, 1
        ret
.no:    xor     eax, eax
        ret

to_number:
        push    rbx
        mov     rbx, rdi
        call    is_number
        test    eax, eax
        jz      .zero
        mov     rdi, rbx
        call    parse_part
        pop     rbx
        ret
.zero:  xor     eax, eax
        pop     rbx
        ret

sum_numbers:
        push    rbx
        xor     ebx, ebx
.next:  cmp     byte [rdi], 0
        je      .done
        cmp     byte [rdi], ' '
        jne     .part
        inc     rdi
        jmp     .next
.part:  call    parse_part
        test    edx, edx
        jz      .next
        add     rbx, rax
        jmp     .next
.done:  mov     rax, rbx
        pop     rbx
        ret

hints: One helper that parses a single part (up to a space or the end) and reports whether it was a number serves all three functions (lesson 8.05).
Subtract `'0'` and compare with 9 using an unsigned jump (`ja`) to reject every character that is not a digit in one test.
unitTests:
test "is it a number"
    is_number("42") == 1
    is_number("-7") == 1
    is_number("0") == 1
    is_number("") == 0
    is_number("-") == 0
    is_number("4x2") == 0
    is_number("12 ") == 0
test "values"
    to_number("1234") == 1234
    to_number("-250") == -250
    to_number("9000000000") == 9000000000
    to_number("abc") == 0
test "sums"
    sum_numbers("10 -3 25") == 32
    sum_numbers("1 two 3") == 4
    sum_numbers("") == 0
    sum_numbers("-") == 0
